title: bug: lease_account during an all-accounts-spent wait never refreshes the seat's lastActivityAt, so a QA seat's REVIEW claim is released by the 30-min self-heal and re-claimed by the next waiting QA wrapper; when the accounts reset, every one of them reviews the same row
description:
Live on 2026-11-03. ACCOUNTS_EXHAUSTED fired at 09:40:05Z with retryAt 11:30Z.
- qa-7328a40d claimed REVIEW task-26d9dc26 in pre-flight at 09:40:37Z. It then sat in the wrapper's MOE_ACCOUNT_WAIT loop: get_account_lease in scripts/moe-agent.sh, twin in moe-agent.ps1. That loop calls moe.lease_account every <= MOE_ACCOUNT_RETRY_SEC (300 s). scripts/CLAUDE.md documents this wait as "the task held".
- The REVIEW self-heal (runBlockedTimeoutSweep in state/sweeps.ts, reviewStaleTimeoutMs 30 min) released the row at 10:13:40Z (WORKER_TIMEOUT), and the record was pruned (WORKER_DISCONNECTED).
- qa-93f9625e's pre-flight claimed the row at 10:13:53Z and was released at 10:48:40Z. qa-af7be174 claimed it at 10:49:02Z and was released at 11:23:41Z.
- At 11:30Z all three wrappers leased acct-1 and launched claude on the same row.
  - Two of them shared the task-keyed jetbrains-gradle lease at 11:31-11:32Z, because acquire is idempotent per task. So the "exclusive" Windows gradle gate could overlap.
  - qa-93f9625e then re-claimed the row at 11:35:57Z, and the other two sessions' verdicts are refused NOT_ALLOWED: wasted reviews.
- The same silence pruned the idle governor's record at 10:13:40Z.

Cause: leaseAccount -> settleLease (state/accountStore.ts) calls touchWorker only when the seat's accountId changes. While every account is spent, each reply carries accountId null, so the wrapper's repeated polls never refresh lastActivityAt. The heartbeat sidecar runs only alongside a live CLI.

Fix (daemon only): count every lease_account call from a registered seat as presence. touchWorker refreshes lastActivityAt on every lease and still writes accountId only when it changes. A waiting wrapper then keeps its held task, as the wrapper contract says. touchWorker already refuses to create an unknown worker or refresh a DEAD one; keep that.

Out of scope: a wrapper-side re-check of the claim before launching after a long wait (a possible follow-up row), and any change to reviewStaleTimeoutMs.
definitionOfDone: Every moe.lease_account call from a registered, non-DEAD seat refreshes that worker's lastActivityAt. This includes the all-spent reply (accountId null with retryAt/retryInSec), a rotation:false reply, and a repeat lease of the same account. accountId is still written only when it changes. An unknown workerId creates no record, and a DEAD worker is not refreshed.

A daemon vitest regression test: a QA worker holds a REVIEW task with lastActivityAt older than reviewStaleTimeoutMs and calls lease_account while every signed-in account is spent. The REVIEW self-heal sweep then leaves the task assigned to that worker. The same sequence without the lease call releases the task, which shows the test discriminates.

docs/MCP_SERVER.md (moe.lease_account) and the Claude account rotation bullet in scripts/CLAUDE.md both state that each lease_account call counts as presence for the calling seat, so a task held through MOE_ACCOUNT_WAIT stays held.
The plan's daemon test command (cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test, or a narrowed suite plus npm run build that the plan justifies) exits 0.

implementationPlan.description:
Tests first (DoD 1, 2; skill test-driven-development). Create packages/moe-daemon/src/state/accountStore.presence.test.ts with the Write tool, never a shell write into the tree (global rail).

Fixture: one ToolTestHarness (src/tools/toolTestHarness.ts) for the file, as in src/state/teamStore.presence.test.ts.
- beforeEach:
  - h.init(). Save the vitest MOE_ACCOUNTS_FILE value, then set process.env.MOE_ACCOUNTS_FILE = path.join(h.testDir, 'machine', 'claude-accounts.json'), as src/tools/accountTools.test.ts does. registryFilePath() reads the env on every call.
  - STALE = new Date(Date.now() - 2 h).toISOString().
  - h.setupMoeFolder(); h.createEpic(); h.createTask({ id: 'task-review', status: 'REVIEW', assignedWorkerId: 'qa-wait' }); h.createWorker({ id: 'qa-wait', currentTaskId: 'task-review', status: 'READING_CONTEXT', lastActivityAt: STALE }).
  - await h.state.load(); vi.spyOn(h.state, 'postToRoleChannel').mockResolvedValue(), which absorbs the all-spent #governors alert.
- afterEach: vi.restoreAllMocks(), restore the env value, h.cleanup().
- Helpers:
  - lease(id = 'qa-wait') = leaseAccountTool(h.state).handler({ workerId: id }, h.state).
  - sweep() = h.state.mutex.runExclusive(() => runBlockedTimeoutSweep(h.state)). This is the real REVIEW self-heal (state/sweeps.ts:493). Never edit sweeps.ts.
  - signIn() = addAccount(file, 'One'), addAccount(file, 'Two'), then recordSignIn(file, 'acct-1' and 'acct-2', 'subscription'), from src/accounts/registry.ts.
  - spendAll() = signIn(), then reportAccountUsageTool(h.state).handler({ accountId, windows: { five_hour: { utilization: 0.95, resetsAt: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 7200, status: 'allowed' } } }, h.state) for both accounts, with NO workerId. A report that names qa-wait learns its account back through settleLease and touches the seat, which would mask the control case.

Cases. Keep these title prefixes, so a FAIL line names its case:
- (p1) all-spent reply:
  - spendAll(); before = Date.now(); reply = await lease().
  - The reply matches { rotation: true, accountId: null, switchAtPercent: 90 }, with a string retryAt and retryInSec > 0.
  - Date.parse(seat.lastActivityAt) >= before.
  - The record has no own accountId key (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call). An absent accountId counts as null, so it is not written.
  - After sweep(), the task matches { status: 'REVIEW', assignedWorkerId: 'qa-wait' } and seat.currentTaskId is 'task-review'.
- (p2) control:
  - spendAll().
  - Guard: Date.now() - Date.parse(seat.lastActivityAt) > h.state.reviewStaleTimeoutMs, and the row is held.
  - sweep() with no lease. The task matches { status: 'REVIEW', assignedWorkerId: null }. This proves the test discriminates.
  - Do not read the seat after this sweep: the Layer-3 prune deletes it.
- (p3) rotation:false reply, with no account list at all:
  - lease() equals { rotation: false, reason: null }.
  - lastActivityAt >= before, and the record has no own accountId key.
  - After sweep(), the row is held.
- (p4) repeat lease of the same account:
  - signIn(). The first lease() returns accountId 'acct-1', and seat.accountId is 'acct-1'.
  - await h.state.updateWorker('qa-wait', { lastActivityAt: STALE }). updateWorker keeps an explicit lastActivityAt.
  - before = Date.now(). The second lease() returns 'acct-1' again; seat.accountId is still 'acct-1' and lastActivityAt >= before.
  - After sweep(), the row is held.
- (p5) unknown seat:
  - spendAll(). lease('qa-ghost') returns accountId null.
  - h.state.getWorker('qa-ghost') is null, and .moe/workers/qa-ghost.json does not exist.
- (p6) DEAD seat:
  - await h.state.createWorker({ id: 'qa-dead', type: 'CLAUDE', projectId: 'proj-test', epicId: 'epic-1', currentTaskId: null, status: 'IDLE' }).
  - updateWorker its lastActivityAt to STALE, THEN its status to 'DEAD'. In that order the DEAD flip keeps the stored time.
  - spendAll(); lease('qa-dead'). The record still matches { status: 'DEAD', lastActivityAt: STALE }.

Red run before step 2. It runs in a snapshot outside the checkout, because the rail allows no npm commands in the shared checkout:
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && S=$(mktemp -d) && git archive HEAD packages/moe-daemon | tar -x -C "$S" && cp packages/moe-daemon/src/state/accountStore.presence.test.ts "$S/packages/moe-daemon/src/state/" && cd "$S/packages/moe-daemon" && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund >/dev/null 2>&1 && NO_COLOR=1 npx vitest run src/state/accountStore.presence.test.ts
It must print Tests 3 failed | 3 passed, failing exactly (p1), (p3) and (p4). The architect's prototype printed exactly that on target 1558f141. Quote those lines in the completion summary.

The fix (DoD 1). It goes in settleLease (packages/moe-daemon/src/state/accountStore.ts:294), edited with the Edit tool. Today it calls touchWorker only when accountId changes; while every account is spent each reply carries accountId null, so the waiting wrapper's polls never refresh the seat.

Call state.touchWorker on EVERY call. Pass { accountId } only when the stored value (absent counts as null) differs, else {}:
const changed = (state.getWorker(workerId)?.accountId ?? null) !== accountId;
await state.touchWorker(workerId, changed ? { accountId } : {});
- Keep the fleet.leases update and the refreshAccounts call as they are.
- Add a short comment saying why: a wrapper in MOE_ACCOUNT_WAIT runs no CLI and no heartbeat sidecar, so its lease polls are its only presence. Without them the REVIEW self-heal released a waiting QA seat's row (2026-11-03). touchWorker creates no record and never refreshes a DEAD one.
- Every leaseAccount return path already goes through settleLease: an invalid list, no accounts, none signed in, all spent, an account chosen. So every reply counts.
- recordAccountReport's learn-back call also goes through settleLease: a report naming a seat whose lease this daemon process forgot. That seat is now refreshed too. That is intended, because only the seat's own wrapper sends such a report.
- Do not edit tools/leaseAccount.ts, state/sweeps.ts or any timeout (governor note; the task's Out of scope).

Error handling: this adds no IO and no failure path. touchWorker already serializes on the reentrant state mutex, returns null for an unknown or DEAD worker, and catches and logs a failed write. So a lease reply never fails because of presence.

Green re-run, in a snapshot:

"$S/repo" && git -C "$S/repo" checkout -q --detach "$H" && for f in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/accountStore.ts packages/moe-daemon/src/state/accountStore.presence.test.ts docs/MCP_SERVER.md scripts/CLAUDE.md; do cp "$f" "$S/repo/$f" || exit 1; done && cd "$S/repo/packages/moe-daemon" && env -i HOME="$HOME" NO_COLOR=1 PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" bash -c 'npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --loglevel=error && npm test && npx tsc --noEmit' && echo 'C1 OK'
- C0: only the 4 planned paths differ from the merge-base with the land target, and the project qualityGate (parity-check, lint) passes.
- C1: the FULL daemon suite (npm test, which is vitest run) plus tsc --noEmit, in a shared clone of HEAD outside the checkout with the 4 files copied in.

Adversarial self-review of this diff only (skill adversarial-self-review):
(1) Concurrency: a deregister racing a lease must not resurrect a DEAD seat. touchWorker re-reads the record under the mutex, and p6 pins it.
(2) Null or absent: an absent accountId must stay absent on a null reply (p1, p3). A changed account must still be written (p4's first lease).
(3) The learn-back side effect: grep the tests that call recordAccountReport or report_account_usage for any assertion that a report leaves lastActivityAt alone.
(4) Load: each lease is one worker-file write and one WORKER_UPDATED. That is at most one per launch, plus one per 300 s while a seat waits.
(5) A MOE_ACCOUNT_RETRY_SEC at or above reviewStaleTimeoutMs/1000 can still lose the row between polls. That stays documented and out of scope.
(6) Nothing in sweeps.ts, leaseAccount.ts or any timeout changed.
If the review changes any file, re-run the step-4 command and submit only that fresh output.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Every moe.lease_account call from a registered, non-DEAD seat refreshes that seat's lastActivityAt, whatever the reply: leased, all-spent (accountId null), rotation:false, or a repeat of the same account. Worker.accountId is written only when it changes. An unknown workerId creates no record, and a DEAD seat is not refreshed. A QA seat waiting in MOE_ACCOUNT_WAIT therefore keeps its REVIEW row through the REVIEW self-heal.
acceptanceCriteria: (p1) After an all-spent lease, a QA seat that was stale past reviewStaleTimeoutMs has a fresh lastActivityAt and no own accountId key. The REVIEW self-heal sweep leaves its row assigned.
(p2) The same fixture without the lease: the sweep releases the row (status REVIEW, assignedWorkerId null).
(p3) A rotation:false lease refreshes lastActivityAt and the row stays held.
(p4) A repeat lease of the same account refreshes lastActivityAt and keeps accountId 'acct-1'.
(p5) A lease for an unknown workerId creates no worker record in memory or on disk.
(p6) A lease for a DEAD seat leaves its stored lastActivityAt and DEAD status unchanged.
On the unfixed source exactly p1, p3 and p4 fail. With the fix the full daemon suite and tsc --noEmit pass.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: settleLease always calls touchWorker and passes { accountId } only when it changed. It is a one-line change, and settleLease is the single funnel for all five leaseAccount return paths, so every reply counts as presence.
Rejected:
- Touching in tools/leaseAccount.ts. It adds a file, and it writes twice when the account changes (handler plus settleLease).
- A wrapper-side moe.heartbeat during MOE_ACCOUNT_WAIT. The task says daemon only; it needs sh and ps1 parity edits; and the lease poll is already a call from the live wrapper.
- Exempting waiting seats inside the REVIEW self-heal. The governor said not to edit sweeps.ts, and it needs new state.
Side effect, accepted: recordAccountReport's learn-back path (a report naming a seat whose lease this daemon process forgot) also refreshes that seat now. Only that seat's wrapper sends it, so it is real presence.
Dependency edge: I added dependsOn task-e3e81c45 as a merge-ordering edge only. DoD 3 must edit scripts/CLAUDE.md line 42, a single physical line, and e3e81c45 edits line 43. A scratch-clone simulation of the landing (target 1558f141 + e3e81c45's hunk, merged with a line-42 edit) gave CONFLICT (content) in scripts/CLAUDE.md. Five workers are idle, so under TURBO this row would otherwise be claimed, and its worktree cut, before e3e81c45 lands. The governor may drop the edge as soon as e3e81c45's completion is on moe/work-2026-10-24 (comment-0994c9ae).
Routing: standard tier, 5 steps and 4 files. Sonnet 5.5 or gpt-6.1-sol at xhigh fits: a one-line fix with a prototyped test.
Epic-final scope: this epic is a rolling bug bucket whose siblings were each QA'd. This row's gate is the full daemon suite plus the quality gate; the review covers this diff.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- touchWorker (state/workerStore.ts:91) runs on the reentrant state mutex, returns null for a missing or DEAD record, and logs and swallows a failed write.
- updateWorker stamps lastActivityAt = now unless the update passes one explicitly. The REVIEW self-heal uses that to keep a crashed QA's time, and test p4 uses it to make a seat stale again.
- REVIEW self-heal: sweeps.ts:493-527. It acts only on a present, non-DEAD owner silent past reviewStaleTimeoutMs; the default equals staleWorkerTimeoutMs, 30 min. The Layer-3 prune at :567 then deletes a stale worker that owns no active task.
- A report_account_usage call that names a workerId learns the lease back through settleLease. Fixtures must therefore seed spent usage with reports that name no seat.
- ToolTestHarness builds its StateManager with the default timeouts. registryFilePath() reads MOE_ACCOUNTS_FILE on every call.
- The wrapper wait loop is scripts/moe-agent.sh get_account_lease (about :9041-9095), with a ps1 twin. It sleeps min(retryInSec, MOE_ACCOUNT_RETRY_SEC), an integer of at least 1, default 300, and leases again. The MOE_ACCOUNT_UNTRUSTED path also leases again after its sleep.
- Daemon doc tests (util/*Docs.test.ts, getCommitScope.test.ts) read docs/MCP_SERVER.md. That is why C1 copies the docs into the snapshot.
planningNotes.risks:
- Merge conflict with e3e81c45 on scripts/CLAUDE.md lines 42 and 43. The dependsOn edge mitigates it; keep the line-42 edit to one inserted clause.
- Presence cost: one worker-file write and one WORKER_UPDATED broadcast per lease. That is at most one per launch, plus one per 300 s per waiting seat.
- An operator MOE_ACCOUNT_RETRY_SEC at or above 1800 still lets the row go between polls. It is documented, not fixed; changing reviewStaleTimeoutMs is out of scope.
- A seat whose record was already pruned stays unregistered: a lease never creates a record, by design.
- The live daemon needs the governor's restage and swap after landing.
- Timing in the tests: a 2 h-old STALE against a 30-min timeout, and lastActivityAt >= before, uses real clocks only. No fake timers are needed, and there is no flake window.
